text:
Asain half squat really fell off for me. 

This used to be a great place to find all the "under the radar" high quality mods cough cough the far from home mod..

But now its just a bunch of generic, redundant, and lazy showcases or countdowns. Its clear that he's just riding the minecraft youtube money wave at this point. 

The pinnacle of minecraft graphics has been the same for many years, with the only major change being ray tracing. So I guess.. thanks for showing me this? Eh.. 

Everyone who actually plays minecraft knows that the game isn't meant to have a high resolution. The textures are supposed to be borderline grainy for the sake of consistency and aesthetically pleasing block borders. 

I mean, let's he honest, most "high res" texture packs are scams anyways. The people who make them often collect thousands of dollars, and then never fully finish the pack, or keep it updated.. 

So I guess thanks for contributing to that as well 

Its just a big machine of internet money, going to people who do little for the community itself. 

There are many people who work very hard to make minecraft a great gaming experience.. most dont get much money at all, and unfortunately, a lot of them don't get noticed, while they have a huge impact behind the scene. Idk just something I noticed from the people I've met while creating FFH. 

I just think its sad that this channel isn't what it used to be. You put a lot of people, including myself, in the spotlight, and doing so, tends to fuel projects, as it did mine. 

But whatever. Now you just run ads on generic minecraft content. Its cool, I understand.

Are you sure it's how much the mods take advantage of your GPU or not and not just how full your VRAM is? In the Optifine screenshot your VRAM is being overloaded by about 2 gigabytes, while in the second screenshot it's not even using close to the full 24GB of it. Having to go to system memory drops performance a LOT, especially if your system memory speed and/or PCI-E is not very fast. I think the difference may just be due to the PBR textures not being included (which takes up VRAM), rather than the mod actually being more efficient at utilising the GPU. 

It's funny how people say you could never need over 8GB VRAM when I see well over that used in: 
- Minecraft
- VRChat
- Cities: Skylines
- Blender
And more. Lots of things can use quite a lot more than 8 or even 12 GB of video memory.

text:
@dripmancer  The problem is not the GPU and not Minecraft. Minecraft is optimized good enough for what it is.

The Problem is the mod used so high resolution textures that filled up the whole GPU memory in no time. Its also not fault of the modder but simply a "Well i did this only for fun to see what happens" mod. It was never intended to be run properly. Its like running Minecraft Vanilla with no Mods at 4K which is good enough, and then using a custom resolution of lets say 16K. No matter in which game you do this, it wont run at all because theres no horsepower of any GPU that can run this (on the 16K example). Same with the textures here, if you use 12800x12800 textures the Vram of your GPU will run full. If you would do this in ANY game it would have the same effect.

So no, you guys are seeing the problem in minecraft, but its not the game its the mod itself that is unusable. The GPU VRAM was absolutely at its end.  Pretty much like eating 3 plates of food an being good, and then wanting to eat 3 x 10 KG bags of Rice at once. The problem is not that your body can't take it, but simply because you have wrong expectations as what you CAN eat at all. 

TLDR : if the GPU had twice as much Vram it would run a lot better (because the "raw" power of the GPU was not at its end) + absolutely insane texture size of the mod which no GPU in the world could ever run, not even in a different game. Its simply bonkers in size and cant be run at all, its just for testing or fun purposes. Thats like wanting to install a 100 GB game on a 80 GB Harddrive, i hope you get the point. Its flawed from the start.

Lastly if you’re not sure whether it’s biome related, can you just plant a shit ton of grass, bushes, and general foliage to see if it looks like it should with the texture pack installed? If it does look right, I’d hazard a guess and say that for the video he used a special world that was generated with a looooot of densely packed foliage and bushes. Could be as simple as that last point now I think of it, it would make sense that he used a specially generated world to show off the graphics and textures as best as possible. Maybe look for a jungle server/world and see how that looks?

Hope some of this helps, like I say I’m not remotely an expert in Minecraft, but I’m just tossing around general troubleshooting steps I’d take if I was trying to figure this out.

text:
Yeah, as others have mentioned, as cool as this is, it doesn't really demonstrate the power of the RTX 3090 Ti, as because this game calculates all of it's effects on the CPU, so does the SEUS PTGI shader pack. I'd argue you would actually gain more frames with a beefier CPU than with a beefy GPU.

You should check out Continuum Graphics, they seem to be developing their own rendering pipeline engine called Focal, which would theoretically offload these graphical effects like shaders and Ray Tracing to the GPU rather than make the CPU calculate them.

I am not sure if it's available for the public right now, but you could try and ask them, your channel is pretty big, so I think they might give you an insider version to show off on your channel if you asked them.

text: 2:43 The problem is the VRAM on the GPU (all 24 gigabytes) is full and the textures are jumping to the system RAM which make the game a ton slower. If you had 2 cards in SLI you might not get double the performance since SLI is basically dead but you might be able to overcome the problem with running out of VRAM.

author: @imadecoy.

text:
Nope, SLI does not multiply vram, the vram is shared across both cards but only the maximum GBs one card has. For example if you have a 4GB + 8GB GPU, only 4GB of the lower GPU will be used in total, and if you have 2 x 8GB then also only 1 x 8 GB are used.

Memory pooling is only possible on Quadro and Titan quards, and even then only working in Linux, not windows.

text: GPU runs faster than cpu. So if same task is run by GPU, it'll be faster. That's what is known as optimization. Minecraft as a game is optimised for every type of pcs while some mods/clients work best with there specific type of GPU. It's just that a game can run smoothly on 1 type of pc (say RTX) or on every pc (even laptops with crappy GPU) with a bit less efficiency. Minecraft is overall optimized for every type cuz of vast userbase.

author: @tsrmmercy836

text:
@abubakrakram6208  Yeah plus the "bus width" of a transfer is much larger in GPUs. RAM can transfer at most 64 bit per channel so 128 bit in dual channel mode. GPUs range from 128-512 so up to 4x more data even at the same clock rate.

Additionally, I'm not actually sure that RAM does a full transaction in a single clock, though thanks to burst mode it should get pretty close. But it could be that RAM uses 1 cycle to write the target address, then 1 cycle to actually read, thus halving the speed. That way, even at the same frequency, different protocols can have vastly different speeds. It's impossible to tell without digging through the exact workings of a single transfer.

text:
2:50 Your graphics card ran out of memory. 3090 Ti has "only" 24 GB of VRAM, and Minecraft needed more than that with those textures and shaders (notice how GPU memory usage is over 24 GB and CPU usage is just around 10%). It had to constantly remove stuff from memory to make room for stuff that didn't fit and load up that stuff to fully render the image, and it had to do all that for every single frame. It's just a lot slower than having everything loaded and ready.

EDIT: As Donghyun Shin pointed out, the data is actually stored in RAM instead of VRAM (graphics card's memory) when it's full, and it takes a lot more time to load textures and stuff from there than from VRAM, and that's what's causing the huge FPS drops.

author: @mangoman7455

text: @mangoman7455  Seus ptgi also has raytracing yeah, but imo it's too shy to add more into the shader. Continuum does some insane shit with simulating a camera, proper wind physics with volumetric fog and clouds, dynamic puddles, and a bunch of more stuff. Though, the main issue is that it's currently forge only due to it using a mod to basically use an external program to do the rendering rather than making minecraft do it.
author: @SwitchyWitch_

text: @SwitchyWitch_  Most mods being used in this video are Fabric mods only, as Fabric tends to be more lightweight and so is much better performance-wise. Not to mention the way it's built basically hands itself to performance mods perfectly while the same cannot be said for Forge
